_note: All rates below are TEAM ASSUMPTIONS, not measured. Ranges come from research/kestrel-real-world-grounding.md section 6. Change them here and re-run; the dashboard compares runs.
business_as_usual: A canceled flight is rebooked on the next Kestrel flight with a free seat, or refunded. Call center and app; the normal wait is 9 minutes, much longer on disruption days. Meal vouchers for delays Kestrel causes of over 3 hours; hotels only for overnight delays Kestrel causes. Fares follow the normal pricing system.

customer_mix._note: TEAM ASSUMPTION, share of Kestrel passengers by group (no public split: research section 5 [GAP]). Dossier: 'Price-conscious travelers: families visiting relatives, students, vacationers, and some small business travelers' plus agencies booking group tickets. Families first (holiday season, Christmas week 97% booked), vacationers next, students on winter break, 'some' business, agencies small but each books a whole group. Shares are passengers, not bookings. Each persona weighs its group's share split evenly over that group's personas.

known_crisis.news: News: ground handling workers (baggage, cleaning, wheelchair help, fueling) at Kestrel Air's contractor in Orlando and Philadelphia plan a 48-hour strike on December 22-23. The contractor says it will bring in replacement staff 'where it can'. The union says the strike 'may be extended'. Talks continue.
known_crisis._severity: SEVERE scenario (team assumption, research section 2: Brussels/Munich-type walkouts, dozens of cancellations a day). Mild scenario for comparison (Charlotte 2024, a few % late): strike_day_share 0.45, cancel 0.05, delay3h 0.15, rebook24 0.75.
known_crisis.strike_news: The ground handling strike is happening now at Orlando and Philadelphia airports. Lines are long; some Kestrel flights are late or canceled.

surprises.title: The engine inspection
surprises.text: The engine inspection. The FAA and the engine maker have told airlines to inspect a part on one engine type. Some of Kestrel's aircraft use it. A passenger's video of mechanics working on an engine at the gate is going round on TikTok. Known: the inspections are a precaution and start this week; no Kestrel aircraft has had a problem with this part. Not known: how many aircraft; how long each check takes; whether any part must be replaced.
surprises._reading: SEVERE as written (team assumption): 75% hear it, 95% of those afraid of flying or on TikTok/Instagram; cancellations x1.5 and 3h+ delays x2 for weeks 3-4. MILD variant: 50% hear it, cancellations x1.1, delays x1.3, week 3 only. Week-4 update supersedes the precaution from week 4 on, so this entry now affects week 3 only.

surprises.title: The engine inspection: three aircraft grounded
surprises.text: The inspections found worn parts on three Kestrel aircraft. They will stay on the ground for about two weeks while new parts arrive. All other aircraft have been cleared to fly. Kestrel will have to cancel or merge some flights in the next two weeks, Thanksgiving week included.
surprises._reading: Team reading of the 14:30 announcement: 3 of 36 aircraft out ~2 weeks = ~8% of flights canceled or merged in weeks 4-5 on top of the normal 2% (cancel_x 5 -> 10%). A leased aircraft (cancel_x 0.8) covers part of the gap.
